q.t: Find the simple interest on ₹1000 at 5% per year for 2 years (in ₹).
q.e: 5% of 1000 is ₹50 for one year. For 2 years: 2 × 50 = 100.

q.t: Which is the formula for simple interest?
q.e: R% of P is the interest for one year (P × R ÷ 100); multiply by T for T years.

q.t: ‘Amount’ means:
q.e: The amount is everything paid back: the money borrowed plus the interest on it.

q.t: Principal = ₹500 and simple interest = ₹50. Find the amount (in ₹).
q.e: Amount = P + SI = 500 + 50.

q.t: Find the simple interest on ₹2000 at 10% per year for 1 year (in ₹).
The money borrowed or lent is called the:
q.e: Principal is the starting sum. Interest is the extra paid for using it.

q.t: Find the simple interest on ₹4000 at 5% per year for 3 years (in ₹).
q.e: One year: 5% of 4000 = 200. Three years: 600.

q.t: In the formula SI = P × R × T ÷ 100, the time T must be in:
q.e: R is a rate per YEAR, so T has to be counted in years to match.

q.t: How many years is 6 months?
q.e: A year has 12 months, so 6 months = 6/12 = 1/2 year.

q.t: A principal of ₹1000 grows to an amount of ₹1200. How much is the interest (in ₹)?
q.e: Interest = amount − principal = 200.

q.t: Find the simple interest on ₹7500 at 8% per year for 2 1/2 years (in ₹).
Find the amount on ₹6000 at 7.5% per year for 4 years (in ₹).
₹5000 earns ₹1200 simple interest in 3 years. Find the rate percent per year.
q.e: Interest per year = 1200 ÷ 3 = 400. 400 out of 5000 = 8%.

q.t: ₹4000 at 6% per year earns ₹960 simple interest. Find the time (in years).
q.e: One year earns 6% of 4000 = 240. 960 ÷ 240 = 4 years.

q.t: A sum earns ₹900 simple interest in 3 years at 5% per year. Find the sum (in ₹).
q.e: In 3 years the interest is 15% of the sum. 15% → 900, so 100% → 6000.

q.t: Find the simple interest on ₹3600 at 10% per year for 9 months (in ₹).
q.e: 9 months = 3/4 year. One year gives 360, so 3/4 of that is 270.

q.t: Find the simple interest on ₹2500 at 12% per year for 146 days (in ₹).
q.e: 146 days = 146/365 = 2/5 year. One year gives 300; 2/5 of 300 = 120.

q.t: Find the amount on ₹9000 at 5% per year for 2 years (in ₹).
q.e: SI = 450 a year × 2 = 900. Amount = 9900.

q.t: Find the simple interest on ₹1250 at 4% per year for 5 years (in ₹).
q.e: 4% for 5 years is 20% in all. 20% of 1250 = 250.

q.t: ₹600 becomes ₹720 in 4 years at simple interest. Find the rate percent per year.
q.e: Interest = 120 in 4 years = 30 a year. 30 out of 600 = 5%.

q.t: A sum of money doubles itself in 10 years at simple interest. Find the rate percent per year.
q.e: To double, the interest must equal the principal: 100% in 10 years = 10% each year.

q.t: A sum amounts to ₹5600 in 4 years at 10% per year simple interest. Find the sum (in ₹).
q.e: In 4 years the interest is 40% of the sum, so the amount is 140% of it. 5600 ÷ 1.4 = 4000.

q.t: In how many years will ₹1600 amount to ₹2000 at 5% per year simple interest?
q.e: Interest needed = 400. One year gives 5% of 1600 = 80. 400 ÷ 80 = 5 years.

q.t: The simple interest on a sum is 9/25 of the sum. The number of years equals the rate percent. Find the rate.
q.e: 9/25 = 36%. Total interest % = R × T = R × R = 36, so R = 6% (for 6 years).

q.t: Find the difference between the simple interest on ₹5000 for 3 years at 8% and at 6% per year (in ₹).
q.e: The rates differ by 2% a year, so the interest differs by 2% of 5000 = 100 a year, or 300 in 3 years.

q.t: A man borrows ₹8000 at 9% per year and lends it at 12% per year, both at simple interest. What is his gain in 2 years (in ₹)?
q.e: He keeps the 3% difference: 3% of 8000 = 240 a year, 480 in 2 years.

q.t: A sum amounts to ₹1150 in 3 years at 5% per year simple interest. Find the sum (in ₹).
q.e: Interest over 3 years = 15% of the sum, so amount = 115% of it. 1150 ÷ 1.15 = 1000.

q.t: Find the simple interest on ₹4500 at 6% per year for 3 years 4 months (in ₹).
q.e: 3 years 4 months = 3 1/3 = 10/3 years. One year gives 270; 270 × 10/3 = 900.

q.t: A sum amounts to ₹2800 in 2 years and to ₹3200 in 4 years at simple interest. Find the sum (in ₹).
q.e: The extra 2 years added ₹400, so interest is ₹200 a year. Sum = 2800 − 2 × 200 = 2400.

q.t: A sum becomes three times itself in 20 years at simple interest. Find the rate percent per year.
q.e: Tripling means the interest is twice the principal = 200% in 20 years = 10% a year.

q.t: A sum amounts to ₹2240 in 2 years and ₹2600 in 5 years at simple interest. Find the rate percent per year.
q.e: 3 extra years add ₹360, so ₹120 a year. Sum = 2240 − 240 = 2000. Rate = 120/2000 = 6%.

q.t: ₹7000 is lent in two parts, one at 6% and the other at 4% per year. The total interest for one year is ₹352. How much was lent at 6% (in ₹)?
q.e: If all were at 4% the interest would be 280. The extra 72 comes from the extra 2% on the 6% part: 72 ÷ 0.02 = 3600.

q.t: At what rate percent per year will the simple interest on a sum be 3/8 of the sum in 5 years?
q.e: 3/8 = 37.5% in total over 5 years, so 37.5 ÷ 5 = 7.5% a year.

q.t: A lends ₹2500 to B and some money to C, both at 7% per year simple interest. After 4 years he receives ₹1120 interest in all. How much did he lend to C (in ₹)?
q.e: Over 4 years the interest is 28% of the total lent. 28% → 1120, so total = 4000. C got 4000 − 2500 = 1500.

q.t: The simple interest on a sum for 5 years at 8% per year is ₹720 less than the sum. Find the sum (in ₹).
q.e: Interest = 40% of the sum, so the gap (sum − interest) is 60% of the sum = 720. Sum = 720 ÷ 0.6 = 1200.

q.t: A sum becomes 7/4 of itself in 6 years at simple interest. Find the rate percent per year.
q.e: Interest = 7/4 − 1 = 3/4 of the sum = 75% in 6 years. 75 ÷ 6 = 12.5% a year.

q.t: Two equal sums are lent at 5% and 7% per year for 3 years. The interests differ by ₹180. Find each sum (in ₹).
q.e: The difference is 2% a year for 3 years = 6% of the sum. 6% → 180, so the sum is 3000.

q.t: A sum triples in 16 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become 5 times itself?
q.e: Tripling needs interest of 2 × the sum (16 years). Five times needs 4 × the sum — twice as much interest, so twice the time: 32 years.

q.t: ₹3000 is lent on 4 February 2023 and returned on 18 April 2023 at 10% per year. Find the simple interest (in ₹).
Ramesh borrowed ₹5000 at 6% per year simple interest. After 2 years he cleared the debt by paying ₹3600 and giving a watch. What was the watch worth (in ₹)?
q.e: SI = 600, so he owed 5600. The watch covered 5600 − 3600 = 2000.
